clue.text: A chorus — one taken from "All hail Jehu" perhaps

indicators.note: taken from says a letter is to be removed from the quoted phrase before it is rearranged
perhaps hints that the quoted phrase is only a jumbled version of what is meant

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A choir sings a greeting to the biblical king Jehu, perhaps with a word dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I (one) from ALL HAIL JEHU and rearrange the remaining ten letters, signalled by 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a hymn of praise, and Handel's famous chorus of that name is a choral setting.

clue.text: Standard of facility illustrated by type of chart

definitions.text: Standard of facility illustrated by type of chart

parts.words: Standard of facility illustrated by type of chart
parts.note: a byword for simplicity, read as a comparison with a round chart cut into slices

explanation.surface: A measure of how easy something is, shown on some kind of graph.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for something very simple ends with the name of a circular chart divided into sectors, hence 'type of chart'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is the proverbial benchmark for something requiring no effort at all, a standard of facility.

clue.text: Shy Liverpudlian sailor's dish

parts.note: to shy is to throw, as is to lob
a Scouse is a native of Liverpool

explanation.surface: A timid person from Liverpool cooking a seaman's meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shy' looks like an adjective (timid) but is the verb to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a meat-and-vegetable stew traditionally eaten by seamen, from which Liverpool's local nickname derives.

clue.text: Casual footwear for couch potatoes

definitions.meaning: idlers who lounge about doing nothing

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both slip-on leather shoes and idle people who laze around the house.

clue.text: Fair decision by referee that led to fighting

definitions.text: Fair decision by referee that led to fighting

parts.words: Fair decision by referee that led to fighting
parts.note: in Greek myth a Trojan prince chose which goddess was fairest, a ruling that brought on the Trojan War

explanation.surface: An official's even-handed ruling sparks a brawl, as at a football match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair' reads as just, but means the most beautiful: the prince awarded the golden apple to Aphrodite, and his reward, Helen, caused the war.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical contest of beauty among Hera, Athena and Aphrodite was settled by a Trojan prince, leading to war with Greece.

clue.text: Encumbers with picnic containers

definitions.meaning: wicker baskets for carrying food outdoors

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb meaning obstructs or hinders and a noun for lidded wicker food baskets.

clue.text: Not attracted by a king

parts.note: to be off something is to have lost one's liking for it

explanation.surface: Someone left cold by a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The king is the eighth-century ruler of Mercia, famous for his dyke along the Welsh border.
explanation.definitionFit: He was an Anglo-Saxon monarch of Mercia, remembered for the earthwork named after him.

clue.text: Pretend to be affected by poet's shrine, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word for the shrine is to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: fane is a literary or poetic word for a temple or shrine

explanation.surface: Faking emotion at a memorial to a writer.
explanation.definitionFit: To feign an illness is to put on a show of suffering from it, pretending it affects you.

clue.text: Device that sounded deeply involved in position-finding

definitions.text: Device that sounded deeply involved in position-finding

parts.words: Device that sounded deeply involved in position-finding
parts.note: a wartime apparatus that measured ocean depths and located submarines by echoes

explanation.surface: Equipment with an impressive, profound voice used in navigation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounded' suggests making a noise, but here means measuring water depth, as an early sonar system did.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the British name for early sonar, which used underwater sound pulses to detect submarines.

clue.text: Where to stick pins in the directors!

parts.note: a peg is a pin of wood or metal
a company's directors together form its board

explanation.surface: A suggestion of sticking pins into the company's executives.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a perforated panel into which pegs or pins are pushed to hang things or keep score.

clue.text: Many, but not all, dairymaids have retired

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the letters are read backwards
only part of the word dairymaids is used, its first six letters

explanation.surface: Lots of milkmaids, though not every one, have stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: Take DAIRYM, the start of 'dairymaids', and read it backwards as 'have retired' says.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means countless or innumerable, so many.

clue.text: Outside church espy lost soul

indicators.note: outside says the rearranged letters go around the abbreviation for church
lost suggests the letters of espy have gone astray and are muddled

explanation.surface: Someone outside a church spots a soul in torment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' signals the anagram, rearranging espy to PSYE; 'Outside' puts those letters round the church abbreviation. 'Soul' is the Greek sense of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek the word means the breath of life, hence the human soul or mind.

clue.text: It reminds us of income heartless men can make

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter is removed, leaving just the outer two
can make says the letters can be formed into something new by rearranging

explanation.surface: Cruel men can earn a living from their income.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' leaves MN from 'men'; add INCOME and rearrange as 'can make' says.
explanation.definitionFit: A memory aid such as a rhyme or acronym exists to remind us of something.

clue.text: Cite indices revealing threat to workers and soldiers, say

definitions.text: threat to workers and soldiers, say

indicators.note: revealing suggests the letters, once rearranged, disclose a different word

explanation.surface: Quoting indexes that show a danger to labourers and troops.
explanation.walkthrough: Workers and soldiers are castes of ants and termites, not people.
explanation.definitionFit: Ants and termites have worker and soldier castes, and a bug-killing chemical threatens such creatures.

clue.text: Balladeer given upper class title in India

parts.note: Bab was the pen-name of W. S. Gilbert for his Bab Ballads

explanation.surface: A singer of ballads honoured with an aristocratic title on the subcontinent.
explanation.walkthrough: W. S. Gilbert, of Gilbert and Sullivan, signed his comic verses 'Bab'.
explanation.definitionFit: In India this was a respectful form of address, like Mr, also used for a clerk.

clue.text: Soprano perhaps lied, leading to tension

parts.note: a lied is a German art song
stress is strain or tension

explanation.surface: A singer told a fib, which caused friction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lied' looks like the past tense of lie, but is the German word for a song.
explanation.definitionFit: A soprano is an example of a female singer.

clue.text: River rose to form a lake

indicators.note: to form says the letters are reshaped into a new word

explanation.surface: A river swells and becomes a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificial lake for storing water supplies is this kind of body.

clue.text: In court for each lie in Room at the Top?

parts.note: up means in court, as when up before the magistrate
per means for each
a story is a fib or lie

explanation.surface: Telling a lie in court, each time, about a novel set high up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Room at the Top' recalls the novel; the question mark allows a top floor, the US spelling of storey.
explanation.definitionFit: An upper floor of a building is literally a room at the top.

clue.text: Moral doubt carrying little weight

definitions.meaning: an old apothecaries' unit of twenty grains

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a pang of conscience and also a tiny apothecaries' weight of twenty grains.

clue.text: It takes ages to accommodate a king in American city

indicators.note: to accommodate means to take in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: yonks is British slang for a very long time, ages
ER stands for Edward Rex, a king

explanation.surface: It takes forever to find a room for a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It takes' is only a link. ER stands for Edward Rex here; a solver may first think of the Queen, but either monarch gives the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a city in New York State, just north of the Bronx.

clue.text: Those retiring usually hit it

parts.note: people going to bed are said to hit this, slang for bed

explanation.surface: People who have stopped work tend to strike something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' suggests leaving work, but means going to bed; to hit the sack is to go to bed, and the sack is also dismissal.
explanation.definitionFit: This is slang for bed, as in the idiom about going to sleep.

clue.text: Run and dive for pearl

parts.note: to tear is to run or rush
to drop is to dive or plunge

explanation.surface: Dash off and plunge into the sea to find a pearl.
explanation.definitionFit: A pear-shaped pearl or gem is described by this shape, like a falling tear.

clue.text: Secure draw at college

parts.note: a tie is a drawn game
up means in residence at university

explanation.surface: Confirming a drawn match while at university.
explanation.walkthrough: UP is British usage for being at university, as in 'up at Oxford'.
explanation.definitionFit: To fasten or make fast with a rope is to secure something.

clue.text: Obliging person identified old coin

definitions.meaning: a former English gold coin bearing St Michael

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a kind helpful person and also a medieval English gold coin showing the archangel Michael.

clue.text: Informer gets six arrested in Norwegian port

indicators.note: arrested means held, so one piece is caught inside another

parts.note: a nark is slang for a police informer
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A grass sees six people taken into custody at a harbour in Norway.
explanation.walkthrough: NARK is British slang for a police informer.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an ice-free harbour town in northern Norway, site of 1940 battles.

clue.text: Base held while soldiers go in over the top

definitions.text: Base held while soldiers go in over the top

parts.words: Base held while soldiers go in over the top
parts.note: soldiers are strips of toast dipped into a boiled egg sitting in a small holder

explanation.surface: Troops charge out of the trenches while a base is defended.
explanation.walkthrough: The military picture misleads: soldiers are fingers of toast dipped into the top of a boiled egg.
explanation.definitionFit: This small holder is the base in which a boiled egg sits while toast fingers are dipped in.

clue.text: Butler detailed men in charge in eloquent language

indicators.note: detailed means having its tail cut off, losing the last letter

parts.note: Rhett Butler is the hero of Gone with the Wind
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers or men

explanation.surface: A manservant itemised staff in authority, speaking grandly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butler' is not a servant but Rhett Butler; 'detailed' (de-tailed) drops his last T.
explanation.definitionFit: This means persuasive or high-flown speech, the art of eloquence.

clue.text: A bit of fencing making one turn ashen

definitions.meaning: a stake forming part of a fence
to go white in the face

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a pointed stake in a fence and also, as a verb, to grow white or wan.

clue.text: A bed of roses by the way can bring comfort

definitions.text: A bed of roses by the way can bring comfort

parts.words: A bed of roses by the way can bring comfort
parts.note: a life of luxury, read as a comfortable road or thoroughfare

explanation.surface: A remark, in passing, that roses can soothe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by the way' looks like an aside, but points to a road: a comfortable thoroughfare.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a life of ease and luxury, a bed of roses.
